name: Requires human gate
description: Estimate whether the proposed next transition/action must stop for explicit human review, approval, or decision.
when_to_use: Use before consequential execution, acceptance, promotion, or transitions whose governing authority may reserve the decision to a human.

existing_approval.description: Whether required approval is already present

requires_human_gate.instructions: Estimate whether an explicit human gate is required before the proposed transition/action may proceed. A gate is warranted only for a specific reason: a consequential choice reserved to humans, a missing required approval, promotion/merge authority, or a policy-defined checkpoint. Do not require a human merely because work is complex, uncertain, or touches a failure. Borderline cases lean false: if no specific rule demands a checkpoint and authority grants the action, the answer is false.

criteria.true: A policy/authority boundary, consequential decision, promotion/merge action, or required checkpoint means execution must stop until a human explicitly reviews, approves, or decides.
criteria.false: The action is within granted authority and no governing rule requires an explicit human checkpoint before proceeding.

changelog.reason: Ben-approved Phase 1D 2026-09-28: instruction rewrite targeting borderline gate calls (lean false absent a specific rule)
